== Biography ==

Flopsy is one of four young rabbits who lived with their Mother in a sand-bank beneath the root of a very large fir-tree. Her siblings are '''[[Mopsy]]''', '''[[Cotton-tail]]''', and '''[[Peter]]'''.

Of the four, Flopsy is distinguished as one of the good little bunnies. She occupied her time gathering blackberries down the lane together with Mopsy and Cotton-tail. For supper, Flopsy had bread, milk, and blackberries.

== Narrative role ==

Flopsy is one of four rabbit siblings, dwelling with her family in a sand-bank beneath the root of a great fir-tree. She is known as a good little bunny—a description that reflects her orderly and obedient nature, which stands in marked contrast to that of her brother [[Peter]].

When their mother ventures to the baker's shop one morning, she instructs her children that they may play in the fields or down the lane, but must avoid Mr. [[McGregor]]'s garden, where their father met with misfortune. Flopsy honors this command faithfully, accompanying her siblings Mopsy and Cotton-tail down the lane to gather blackberries—a task the three well-behaved rabbits pursue without incident.

While Peter, heedless of his mother's warning, sneaks into Mr. McGregor's garden and returns sickened by his transgression, Flopsy remains safe and content. She enjoys bread and milk and blackberries for supper—the quiet reward of obedience—while Peter is administered camomile tea and put to bed.

== Personality ==

Flopsy embodies goodness and obedience. The text explicitly describes her as a "good little bunny," a characterization that reveals something essential about her nature. She is the sort of rabbit who takes her mother's instructions seriously and acts upon them with quiet diligence.

Her temperament is dutiful and industrious. When set to gather blackberries, she pursues the task with her siblings, working steadily alongside them. There is a steadiness in her nature, a willingness to do what is asked of her without hesitation or complaint.

Flopsy's obedience springs from respect for her mother's wisdom and acceptance of the boundaries established for her protection. This trust and compliance are rewarded in simple but genuine comfort—the bread, milk, and blackberries that comprise her supper, eaten in contentment and security.

Her character is further illuminated by implicit contrast with her brother Peter's recklessness and disobedience. Where he defies their mother's instruction and ventures into danger, Flopsy's compliance and prudence lead to safety and satisfaction.

== Trivia ==

Flopsy's distinguishing trait among her siblings is her consistent good behavior and obedience to her mother's wishes. On the day of the story, she and her sister Mopsy, along with their brother Cotton-tail, gathered blackberries down the lane—a productive errand that earned her a supper of bread, milk, and blackberries.
